The compilers' choices matter in proportion to the program's control and allocation, not its arithmetic or its builtins.
The gap is in hazel-jit's calls (an array per call of a function of a tuple), its generic equality and its recursion; the five changes below address exactly those.
A frame 45 times faster; the view's work alone 134 times, in the same process.
Compiling pays most where the interpreter takes many small steps: a view over a large value is such a case.

Whole-program inlining helps; OCaml's runtime library, written in JS, can cost more than the program.
